description: Reference treatments reverse-engineered from the ten Extra Sensory II Vivify maps, recording how each map's central idea, motifs, key moments and possession follow from its song, for use as concept examples by an authoring agent.
rights: Local study only; descriptions and paraphrases, no lyrics, note arrays or assets.

source.mapper: Droobix (TheGoodBoi); original chart by Ján Ilavský

song.mood: bright, driving electronic dance track from the game's own 2018 soundtrack

entries.title: Noclipping out of an old build
entries.central_idea: The map pretends to be a corrupted early build of Beat Saber; mid-song the player falls out of the game world into a VHS-filtered Backrooms-style space and is snapped back into the normal game at the end.

moments: chart dropout at beats 80-111 used as the fall out of the world
late sparse phrase (272-298) used for the entity pass and return
mood: the song's upbeat, familiar character makes the corruption read as wrong
found-footage unease layered over a cheerful track
lyrics: instrumental; the theme comes from the song's history as one of the game's first tracks
grounding.notes: Grounded in what the song is (an original Beat Saber track with a known original chart) rather than in its sound; the mapper's description frames it as an excavated old build, and the Kane Pixels credit points to The Backrooms.

buildability.notes: Tier 1 for the parented environment and the room from primitives; tier 2 for the VHS and static-note shaders and camera composition; tier 3 only for the character head model and a textured Backrooms room.

grounded.why: Follows from the song's history as an original Beat Saber track more than from its sound.

one_idea.why: One premise, a broken old build the player falls out of, carries every event.

develops.why: VHS, static notes and the removed world escalate and resolve in a return at the end.

readable.why: Chart is about 1.2 NPS, though static-rendered notes add noise for about 160 beats.

buildable.why: Mostly primitives and two post-process shaders; only one character model.

song.mood: ominous, swelling ambient cue that signals the approaching supernova

entries.title: One Outer Wilds loop
entries.central_idea: The song becomes one time loop of Outer Wilds: the player wakes inside the suit, drifts through the solar system, sees the sun explode, dies, watches their own run replay in reverse, and wakes again.

moments: the song's role as the supernova warning places the explosion near its climax (beat 205, 96 s)
the long note-free second half gives room for death and memory
mood: dread and awe at the end of the system
lyrics: instrumental; the theme is the game's 22-minute loop that ends in a supernova
grounding.notes: Every set piece is a step of the loop the cue scores in the game, including the reverse flashback of the last life and the wake-up gasp.

development.memory (262-308.75): frames played back in reverse at shrinking intervals

buildability.notes: Tier 2 for the render-texture recorder, memory panel, death and bloom shaders and HUD materials; tier 3 for the ship, planets and supernova art.

grounded.why: Stages exactly what this cue accompanies in its game, including the flashback.

one_idea.why: One loop from waking to waking again organises the whole map.

develops.why: Recorded frames and HUD set up early pay off in the death and replay.

readable.why: 32 notes at 0.5 NPS; nothing competes with them.

buildable.why: The recorder is code, but the solar system, ship and supernova need modelled art.
